subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should this remain one umbrella macOS Gateway stability issue, or should maintainers split the remaining work into a memory/RSS soak investigation and a restart-aware cron failure reporting design?
rationale: Current main contains partial fixes, but the remaining behavior spans memory backend ownership, macOS launchd validation, and failure-alert semantics that automation should not choose without maintainer direction.

options.title: Keep umbrella open for maintainer validation
options.body: Use this issue as the coordinating tracker until a current-main macOS soak and failure-alert design decision identify the exact remaining fix boundary.

options.title: Split into two focused trackers
options.body: Create one tracker for memory/RSS growth under memory-core/QMD/dreaming and one for external or restart-aware cron failure reporting, then cross-link this issue as the umbrella context.

options.title: Close after proven soak
options.body: Close only if a maintainer-run current-main or shipped-release soak reproduces neither the memory growth nor the silent cron failure under the reported workload.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella open for maintainer validation
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the coordinating tracker until a current-main macOS soak and failure-alert design decision identify the exact remaining fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the linked memory FD fix and have concrete recent history in the memory watcher area most likely to anchor the first validation pass.
